statement: 26 of 26 points of the dependency chain are present in the built projection, across 84 probes; 57 assets and 73 evidenced edges

chain.statement: Payments API: down 3 release → 6 process → 3 provider → 3 operation → 9 algorithm → 2 key → 3 key_provider → 1 certificate → 2 endpoint; up 1 system

capability.statement: OpenSSL 3.0.11: 6 capability(ies), 3 observed use(s) from 2 layer(s), 4 listed and never used, 1 used without being listed
capability.rule: a capability is what the provider says it can do; usage is an operation with an evidence class, and one never becomes the other

findings.reason: the sources disagree about which version is deployed; the disagreement is the finding, not the newest value

conflicts.rule: a conflict keeps every source; a CBOM that resolves it by precedence has thrown away the one fact worth reporting

change.rule: a dependency that stops being observed is superseded, not deleted: what the estate used to depend on is part of the answer

lifecycle.statement: 8 dependency edge(s): ACTIVE 1, CHANGED 2, SUPERSEDED 1, REMOVED 1, UNKNOWN 3
lifecycle.rule: SUPERSEDED and REMOVED are states, not deletions: an edge that stopped being observed is kept with its last value and the evidence that said so

provider_impact.statement: OpenSSL 3.0.11 3.0.11 vs advisory 3.0.11: 1 process(es), 1 application(s), 1 business system(s), 3 operation(s) affected
not_proven: that every affected asset was discovered: the answer is bounded by the applications that were inspected
that the version the inventory records is the version running: a process map and an SBOM can disagree, and that disagreement is reported as a conflict rather than resolved here

advisories.statement: CVE-2026-0001: 1 firmware record(s), 1 device(s), 1 application(s) behind them

limits: the fixture is the bank's own path: every shape is real, the rows are not
the provider's operation list is what a runtime probe saw once; a second sample could add an operation and no sample can remove one
a static hit names a file, an API and a line; it never proves the branch ran
the key record is a reference and its metadata: nothing here proves which key produced a signature, and nothing here would hold the key if it could
the KMS answer is the strongest single answer in the estate, not the strongest answer per application
coverage is arithmetic on what the collectors reported; it cannot see an application that was never scanned
a capability is the provider's own list, self-reported; it says what the build was compiled with and nothing about which of those paths a caller took
the lifecycle compares two projections: a dependency that moved between collections the bank never ran is not visible here
the advisory answers are keyed on the names the estate holds — a firmware version nobody recorded cannot match a CVE
the edge audit counts records, not truth: an edge can carry every field and still be wrong, which is what the conflict and change queries are for
